simple.meaning: אַסִּיר (ʼaççîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “prisoner.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַסִּיר (H616) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 79:11, with occurrences in Psalms, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַסִּיר (H616) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַסִּיר (H616) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַסִּיר (ʼaççîyr) / H616 is traced through Psalms 79:11, Isaiah 10:4, Isaiah 24:22, Isaiah 42:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before you.

timeline.evidenceText: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before you.
They will only bow down under the prisoners,
They will be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and will be shut up in the prison; and after many days they will be visited.

definitions.full: H616. assir אַסִּיר noun [masculine] mostly collective prisoners (according to Ol § 185 a corruption of אָסִיר , compare Lag BN 110 ) taken in battle Isa 10:4 (Lag Symm i. 105; GGA 1884, 259 reads אֹסִיר חַת etc., Osiris is broken , but compare Che critical note .), 24:22 (simile of judgment upon kings of earth); 42:7 (|| חשֶׁךְ ישְׁבֵי ; reference to exiled Israel, but see also Hi Che Di); 1Chr 3:17 אַסִּר יְכָנְיָה בְּנֵי probably = sons of Jeconiah the captive (yet note omission of article) so Be Zö Öttli and others; ᵑ9 ᵐ5 translated as proper name
